title: Review coding with the Coding Review drawer

claims.claim: It opens as a right-side drawer with the clinical summary on the left, the billing codes on the right
... and every override attributed and logged.

checks.note: would hold if overrides made in the drawer were recorded

claims.finding: The drawer's only override is 'Save anyway' on the duplicate-claim dialog (force: true to update-claim-codes, CodingReviewDrawer.tsx:461-492); the drawer writes no override record. Recorded coding-fact overrides happen on the claim page's manual paths (BillingClaimDetailPage.tsx:794-870 via mark-claim-submitted).
claims.proposed_text: Coding-fact overrides confirmed on Mark as Submitted, Fix & Resubmit or Send Fax are attributed and recorded in the claim's history.

claims.claim: You have the biller role, or admin.
claims.finding: The Work Queue route is gated by the "Billing Operations" feature (RequireFeature + FeatureAccess, frontend/src/user-routes.tsx:966-975), not a biller/admin role check; role-to-feature mapping is tenant data.
claims.proposed_text: You have access to Billing Operations.

claims.claim: A claim exists on the encounter — the drawer is reachable only when the row has a claim. From /facility/{facility_uuid}/billing/work-queue, click Review on any row that has a claim. The drawer slides in from the right.
Use ← / → at the top to move to the previous or next claim in the current queue without closing the drawer.
The header shows the patient, DOS, payer, rendering clinician, and a timely-filing badge (Nd to file or Nd PAST DEADLINE).
If the visit is not signed, a red banner across the top says so

claims.claim: — the claim cannot be submitted until the provider signs.
claims.finding: Not provable from code. New Claim offers only locked visits (frontend/src/pages/NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:158-161), but no submit edge path (submitToStedi.ts, submit-claim, submit-to-stedi, biller-submit-claim-onbehalf) checks visit_locked, and Mark as Submitted / Send Fax do not either. Whether an existing claim on an unsigned visit can be submitted needs a browser/DB test.

claims.claim: Left — Clinical Summary. Read-only cards pulled from the progress note that supports this claim: Wound Assessment (section 7), Procedures & Supplies (section 11), Objective Assessment (section 4), Provider Attestation (section 17).
View Full Note opens the PDF in a new tab.
Coding Review now resolves the correct note for a claim across three ID namespaces, not just one ... coverage on the reachable set jumped from 60 to 174 of 461 clinical notes on production.

checks.pattern: REACHABLE coverage with the three tiers below: 174 of 461.

claims.claim: Before the fix, ~87% of claims had no note surface in the drawer even when a signed note existed

checks.note: would hold if the measurement were of claims

claims.finding: The measurement is of notes, not claims: 60 of 461 visit_form + initial_evaluation notes matched, 'so for the other 401 the coder sees no note' (frontend/src/utils/billing/resolveProgressNoteFilePath.ts:7-10). 401/461 is 87% of notes.
claims.proposed_text: Before the fix, the drawer could find only 60 of 461 clinical notes on production; for the other 401 (about 87%) the coder saw no note.

proposed_checks.pattern: the other 401 the coder sees no note

claims.claim: Right — Billing Codes. Editable: Place of Service (two-digit code, e.g. 12)
Billing Codes (procedures with modifiers, units, and diagnoses; each procedure line carries its own diagnosis pointers)

checks.note: would hold if each line kept its own diagnoses

claims.finding: On save the drawer gives every procedure line the full list of the claim's ICD-10 codes (frontend/src/utils/billing/codingReviewAdapters.ts:67-79: icd_codes: icdCodes for every line); the code entry has no per-line diagnosis control.
claims.proposed_text: Billing Codes (procedures with modifiers, units and charges, plus the claim's ICD-10 diagnoses; on save every procedure line points to all listed diagnoses)

claims.claim: Expected Total rolls up automatically from the line charges
Claim Status inline dropdown mirrors the Work Queue value
Red — validation errors: The claim payload is structurally broken (missing subscriber, missing service line, etc.). Submission is blocked until you fix them.

checks.note: would hold if the red banner checked payload structure

claims.finding: The only error-severity rule is 'Procedure/supply codes present with no supporting ICD-10 diagnosis — guaranteed denial.' (frontend/src/utils/billing/codingValidation.ts:41-42). The drawer has no submit action, and Save is not blocked by it (CodingReviewDrawer.tsx:803).
claims.proposed_text: Red — error: procedure or supply codes with no ICD-10 diagnosis on the claim (a guaranteed denial). Fix it before submitting; Save stays available.

proposed_checks.pattern: message: 'Procedure/supply codes present with no supporting ICD-10 diagnosis — guaranteed denial.',

claims.claim: Yellow — warnings: Codes look inconsistent with the visit (diagnosis not linked to a line, modifier missing, out-of-range units). Advisory only; save and submit are still available.

checks.note: would hold if warnings covered diagnosis links or units

claims.finding: The warnings are: E/M with procedures but no modifier 25; a line with a $0.00 charge; a skin substitute without KX (frontend/src/utils/billing/codingValidation.ts:31-65). No diagnosis-link or units warning exists.
claims.proposed_text: Yellow — warnings: an E/M code billed with procedures but no modifier 25, a line with a $0.00 charge, or a skin substitute without the KX modifier. Advisory only; Save stays available.

proposed_checks.pattern: billed with procedures but missing modifier 25.`,
missing KX modifier — most LCDs require it.`,

claims.claim: Yellow items are worth resolving but do not block save.
Set Place of Service if the wrong value is on the claim (12 for home, 11 for office, etc.).
Adjust the code list on the right — add or remove procedures, correct modifiers, correct units, and edit the diagnosis links on each line.

checks.note: would hold if diagnosis links were per line

claims.finding: There is no per-line diagnosis link in the drawer; every line gets all ICD-10 codes on save (frontend/src/utils/billing/codingReviewAdapters.ts:68-75).
claims.proposed_text: Adjust the code list on the right — add or remove procedures and diagnoses, correct modifiers and units.

claims.claim: Check Expected Total — that number is what the payer will see. If it is $0.00, the claim will fail to submit; add prices in Charge Master first.

checks.pattern: message: `Claim total is $${claimTotal.toFixed(2)} — nothing is being billed. Add charges in Charge Master.`,

claims.claim: Set Claim Status if it changed (Ready, Hold, Flag Clinical, Needs Coding, etc.).
Click Save, or Save & Next (Ctrl+Enter) to move to the next claim in one keystroke.
Add a Biller Note if the team needs context on what you changed. Notes save separately from codes.
Save — Persists code, POS, and diagnosis-pointer changes to the claim. Enabled only when you have edited something.

checks.note: would hold if per-line pointers were edited and saved

claims.finding: Save sends codes and POS to update-claim-codes and is enabled only when dirty; there are no per-line diagnosis pointers to change — every line is saved with all ICD-10 codes (codingReviewAdapters.ts:75).
claims.proposed_text: Save — Persists code, diagnosis and POS changes to the claim. Enabled only when you have edited something.

claims.claim: Save & Next (Ctrl+Enter) — Saves and jumps to the next queue row without closing the drawer.
Flag for Clinical — Marks the claim's status as Flag Clinical and sends the row back to the clinical team for review.
Edit in Full Form — Opens /billing/new?editClaimId=… — the same claim, expanded into the full submit page.
Close — Closes the drawer. Unsaved edits are discarded.

When a code triggers a coding-fact finding — MUE unit ceilings, unusual Place of Service, mutually exclusive procedures — the submitter does not silently accept it, and it also does not refuse outright. Instead: Submit stops, and a modal names every finding in the biller's words ("CPT 97597 units exceed CMS MUE of 3 per DOS").

checks.note: would hold if Submit to Stedi still stopped on coding facts

claims.finding: Since 2026-09-02 coding facts are warning-only on Submit to Stedi: they never stop the claim (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/submitToStedi.ts:388-445). The manual paths stop with a browser confirm dialog, not a modal (BillingClaimDetailPage.tsx:801-805, :850-856). The checks are MUE 0, place-of-service restriction and MUE unit caps (validateCodingFacts.ts:115-160); there is no mutually-exclusive-procedure check.
claims.proposed_text: Coding-fact findings (MUE 0 codes, place-of-service restrictions, MUE unit caps) never stop Submit to Stedi; they are reported as warnings. On Mark as Submitted, Fix & Resubmit and Send Fax, a confirm dialog lists every finding before you proceed.

proposed_checks.pattern: `This claim has ${issues.length} coding issue${issues.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} that would block electronic submission:\n\n` +

claims.claim: You either fix the codes and try again, or confirm the override — "Submit it anyway".
claims.finding: No 'Submit it anyway' control exists. The Send Fax confirm ends '<action> anyway? Your confirmation will be recorded on the claim.' with action 'Fax it' (BillingClaimDetailPage.tsx:752, :801-805); Mark as Submitted / Fix & Resubmit use buildMarkSubmittedConfirmMessage. All are browser OK/Cancel dialogs.
claims.proposed_text: You either fix the codes and try again, or click OK in the confirm dialog (for a fax it asks "Fax it anyway? Your confirmation will be recorded on the claim.").

proposed_checks.pattern: `${action} anyway? Your confirmation will be recorded on the claim.`,

claims.claim: If you confirm, the submission proceeds AND a row is written to claim_status_history with the method (electronic / manual / fax / resubmit), the codes overridden, and who overrode them.

checks.note: would hold if an electronic override method were recorded

claims.finding: Recorded methods are manual, resubmit and fax only (backend/supabase/functions/mark-claim-submitted/logic.ts:10-16); the row is written by mark-claim-submitted with the user id and the overridden codes (index.ts:141-151). Electronic submissions record no override because the findings no longer stop them.
claims.proposed_text: If you confirm on Mark as Submitted, Fix & Resubmit or Send Fax, a row is written to claim_status_history with the method (manual / resubmit / fax), the codes overridden, and who confirmed.

claims.claim: The same check now runs on all four submission paths — Submit to Stedi, Mark as Submitted, Fix & Resubmit, and Send Fax — so a biller cannot walk around the electronic gate by faxing the claim off-system. Every override reads back as an attributed decision on the claim, not a silent bypass.

checks.note: would hold if there were still an electronic gate to walk around

claims.finding: The check runs on all four paths, but on Submit to Stedi it is warning-only since 2026-09-02 (submitToStedi.ts:388-445), so there is no electronic gate; the manual paths are now the stricter ones. Electronic findings are logged, not recorded as attributed overrides.
claims.proposed_text: The same check runs on all four submission paths. On Submit to Stedi it is a warning only and does not stop the claim; on Mark as Submitted, Fix & Resubmit and Send Fax the biller confirms each finding and the confirmation is recorded on the claim.

claims.claim: The row in the Work Queue reflects the new codes on refresh (every 2 minutes, or Refresh to force).
Troubleshooting: Left panel says "No note" — The claim was created manually, or the note lives in a namespace outside the three tiers.
claims.finding: The texts are "No signed note found for this visit." (frontend/src/components/billing/CodingReviewNoteLink.tsx:33) and, for a manual claim, "No visit data — claim was created manually" (CodingReviewDrawer.tsx:686).
claims.proposed_text: Left panel says "No signed note found for this visit." or "No visit data — claim was created manually".

proposed_checks.pattern: No signed note found for this visit.
No visit data — claim was created manually

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: "VISIT NOT SIGNED" banner — The progress note is a draft or in-progress — Use Notify on the Work Queue row.
Troubleshooting: Yellow warning about diagnosis pointers — A procedure line has no diagnosis linked, or points to a diagnosis you removed — Reassign the pointer on the line.

checks.note: would hold if the drawer's validator warned about diagnosis pointers

claims.finding: No diagnosis-pointer warning or per-line pointer control exists in the drawer (frontend/src/utils/billing/codingValidation.ts has no such rule; BillingCodeEntry.tsx only has a drag-and-drop PointerSensor). The related check is the red error 'Procedure/supply codes present with no supporting ICD-10 diagnosis' (codingValidation.ts:41-42).
claims.proposed_text: Red error about a missing diagnosis — procedure codes are on the claim with no ICD-10 code. Add the diagnosis; every line will point to it.

proposed_checks.pattern: message: 'Procedure/supply codes present with no supporting ICD-10 diagnosis — guaranteed denial.',

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: Expected Total is $0.00 — The line has no price in facility_charge_master — Open Charge Master for the facility and add the price.

checks.note: would hold if adding the Charge Master price fixed the drawer's total

claims.finding: Adding the price in Charge Master does not change this claim: the drawer shows the stored line charges and never reads Charge Master (CodingReviewDrawer.tsx:241-262, :399-406). The biller must also put the price on the line.
claims.proposed_text: Expected Total is $0.00 — the line has no charge. Add the price in Charge Master for future claims, and type it into this line's charge box, then Save.

claims.claim: Troubleshooting: Save button disabled — You have not edited anything, or the claim row failed to load — Reopen the drawer, or use Edit in Full Form.
